q: Mechanisms of breathing are for gas exchange which is the uptake of oxygen from environment and the elimination of ____ from the body.
e: Mechanisms of breathing are for gas exchange which is the uptake of oxygen from environment and the elimination of carbon dioxide from the body. Carbon dioxide is used in photosynthesis and produced by respiration and combustion. Gas exchange is uptake of oxygen and removal of carbon dioxide.

q: The general body surface of most animals lacks sufficient surface area to exchange gases for the whole organism. To solve this limitation is the evolution of respiratory or ____.
e: The general body surface of most animals lacks sufficient surface area to exchange gases for the whole organism. To solve this limitation is the evolution of respiratory or breathing organs. A large surface area speeds diffusion, which is why lungs, gills, and leaves are folded or flattened.

q: These organs are extensively folded or branched thereby enlarging the available surface area for gas exchange such as gills, tracheae, ____ and other modified structures.
e: These organs are extensively folded or branched thereby enlarging the available surface area for gas exchange such as gills, tracheae, lungs and other modified structures. Lungs are the main terrestrial organs of gas exchange. Gas exchange is uptake of oxygen and removal of carbon dioxide.

q: ____ are gas exchange organs for aquatic animals.
e: Gills are gas exchange organs for aquatic animals. Gills are folded, water-suspended surfaces used by many aquatic animals. Gas exchange is uptake of oxygen and removal of carbon dioxide.

q: Gills are outfolding of body surfaces that are suspended in ____.
e: Gills are outfolding of body surfaces that are suspended in water. Water is the essential solvent of cells and a raw material of photosynthesis. Gills are folded, water-suspended surfaces used by many aquatic animals.

q: Aquatic animals that use gills are polychaetes (marine worms of the phylum Annelida), crustaceans, sea stars and ____.
e: Aquatic animals that use gills are polychaetes (marine worms of the phylum Annelida), crustaceans, sea stars and fish. Fish typically use gills; aquatic turtles more often use lungs and accessory surfaces. Many polychaete worms use gills in water.

q: Each gill arch has two rows of gill filaments, composed of flattened plates called ____.
e: Each gill arch has two rows of gill filaments, composed of flattened plates called lamellae. Dichotomous means divided into two parts, from Greek.

q: Blood flowing through capillaries within the lamellae picks up oxygen from the ____.
e: Blood flowing through capillaries within the lamellae picks up oxygen from the water. Water is the essential solvent of cells and a raw material of photosynthesis. Blood carries oxygen bound to haemoglobin.

q: The counter current flow of water and blood causes the continuous diffusion of oxygen from the water into the blood over the entire length of a ____.
e: The counter current flow of water and blood causes the continuous diffusion of oxygen from the water into the blood over the entire length of a capillary. Blood carries oxygen bound to haemoglobin. Counter-current flow in fish gills keeps a gradient so more oxygen is extracted.

q: Although the most familiar respiratory structure among terrestrial animals is the lungs, some use tracheae (in insects), book lungs (in spiders and scorpions). Others use ____ (in earthworms, frogs and toads).
e: Although the most familiar respiratory structure among terrestrial animals is the lungs, some use tracheae (in insects), book lungs (in spiders and scorpions). Others use skin (in earthworms, frogs and toads). Skin is a surface for some heat exchange and a barrier, but most large animals also need lungs or gills. Book lungs are stacked gas-exchange plates in some arachnids.

q: Frogs and toads often use the lining of the ____.
e: Frogs and toads often use the lining of the buccal cavity. Buccal cavity is the biological term this statement needs.

q: The lungs are enclosed in the chest or thorax by the rib cage and a muscular sheet of tissue called the ____.
e: The lungs are enclosed in the chest or thorax by the rib cage and a muscular sheet of tissue called the diaphragm. The diaphragm contracts and flattens to increase thorax volume during inhalation. Lungs are the main terrestrial organs of gas exchange.

q: Joining each rib to the next are two sets of muscles called ____.
e: Joining each rib to the next are two sets of muscles called intercostal muscles. Intercostal muscles move the ribs to change thorax volume during breathing. Dichotomous means divided into two parts, from Greek.

q: The diaphragm separates the contents of the thorax from the ____.
e: The diaphragm separates the contents of the thorax from the abdomen. The diaphragm contracts and flattens to increase thorax volume during inhalation.

q: It is not flat, but a shallow dome shape, with a fibrous middle part forming the 'roof' of the dome, and muscular edges forming the ____.
e: It is not flat, but a shallow dome shape, with a fibrous middle part forming the 'roof' of the dome, and muscular edges forming the walls. Walls is the biological term this statement needs.

q: When breathing in, air enters the nose or mouth and passes down the windpipe or ____.
e: When breathing in, air enters the nose or mouth and passes down the windpipe or trachea. The trachea is the airway that carries air toward the bronchi. An extra chromosome 21 produces Down's syndrome.

q: The trachea splits into two tubes called the ____, one leading to each lung.
e: The trachea splits into two tubes called the bronchi, one leading to each lung. The trachea is the airway that carries air toward the bronchi. Dichotomous means divided into two parts, from Greek.

q: Each bronchus divides into smaller and smaller tubes called ____, eventually ending at microscopic air sacs, called alveoli.
e: Each bronchus divides into smaller and smaller tubes called bronchioles, eventually ending at microscopic air sacs, called alveoli. Bronchioles are the finer airways that end in alveoli. Alveoli are tiny lung sacs with a huge surface for diffusion of gases.

q: The walls of trachea and bronchi contain rings of gristle or ____, which support the airway and keep them open when breathing.
e: The walls of trachea and bronchi contain rings of gristle or cartilage, which support the airway and keep them open when breathing. Cartilage keeps airways such as the trachea open. The trachea is the airway that carries air toward the bronchi.

q: The inside of the thorax is separated from the lungs by two thin, moist membranes called the ____.
e: The inside of the thorax is separated from the lungs by two thin, moist membranes called the pleural membranes. Pleural membranes and fluid let the lungs slide as the thorax changes volume. Lungs are the main terrestrial organs of gas exchange.

q: Between the two membranes is a space called the pleural cavity, filled with a thin layer of liquid called ____.
e: Between the two membranes is a space called the pleural cavity, filled with a thin layer of liquid called pleural fluid. Pleural membranes and fluid let the lungs slide as the thorax changes volume. Dichotomous means divided into two parts, from Greek.

q: ____ means moving air in and out of the lungs.
e: Ventilation means moving air in and out of the lungs. Ventilation is moving air or water across the gas-exchange surface. Lungs are the main terrestrial organs of gas exchange.

q: Ventilation depends on the fact that thorax is an ____ cavity.
e: Ventilation depends on the fact that thorax is an airtight cavity. Ventilation is moving air or water across the gas-exchange surface.

q: When breathing, the volume of the thorax change, which alters the pressure inside it. This causes air to move in or out of the ____.
e: When breathing, the volume of the thorax change, which alters the pressure inside it. This causes air to move in or out of the lungs. Lungs are the main terrestrial organs of gas exchange.

q: During inhalation, external intercostal muscles ____ and internal intercostal muscles relax.
e: During inhalation, external intercostal muscles contract and internal intercostal muscles relax. Intercostal muscles move the ribs to change thorax volume during breathing.

q: During exhalation, external intercostal muscles relax and internal intercostal muscles ____.
e: During exhalation, external intercostal muscles relax and internal intercostal muscles contract. Intercostal muscles move the ribs to change thorax volume during breathing.

q: During inhalation, the rib cage causes upward and ____ movement.
e: During inhalation, the rib cage causes upward and outward movement. Outward is the biological term this statement needs.

q: During exhalation, the rib cage causes downward and ____ movement.
e: During exhalation, the rib cage causes downward and inward movement. Inward is the biological term this statement needs.

q: During inhalation, muscles of diaphragm ____.
e: During inhalation, muscles of diaphragm contract. The diaphragm contracts and flattens to increase thorax volume during inhalation.

q: During exhalation, muscles of diaphragm ____.
e: During exhalation, muscles of diaphragm relax. The diaphragm contracts and flattens to increase thorax volume during inhalation.

q: During inhalation, diaphragm becomes ____.
e: During inhalation, diaphragm becomes flattened. The diaphragm contracts and flattens to increase thorax volume during inhalation.

q: During exhalation, diaphragm goes back to its normal ____ shape.
e: During exhalation, diaphragm goes back to its normal dome shape. The diaphragm contracts and flattens to increase thorax volume during inhalation.

q: During inhalation, chest ____ in volume.
e: During inhalation, chest increases in volume. Increases is the biological term this statement needs.

q: During exhalation, chest ____ in volume.
e: During exhalation, chest decreases in volume. Decreases is the biological term this statement needs.

q: During inhalation, chest ____ in pressure.
e: During inhalation, chest decreases in pressure. Decreases is the biological term this statement needs.

q: During exhalation, chest ____ in pressure.
e: During exhalation, chest increases in pressure. Increases is the biological term this statement needs.

q: During inhalation, air ____ into the lungs.
e: During inhalation, air enters into the lungs. Lungs are the main terrestrial organs of gas exchange.

q: During exhalation, air ____ out of the lungs.
e: During exhalation, air leaves out of the lungs. Lungs are the main terrestrial organs of gas exchange.
